english: In a town of $N$ people a rumour spreads in such a way that the rate of increase of the number $R(t)$ of people who have heard it is proportional to the product of $R(t)$ and the number of people who have not heard it, $t$ being the time in hours. hindi: $N$ लोगों के एक नगर में एक अफवाह इस प्रकार फैलती है कि उसे सुन चुके लोगों की संख्या $R(t)$ के बढ़ने की दर, $R(t)$ तथा उसे न सुनने वाले लोगों की संख्या के गुणनफल के समानुपाती है, जहाँ $t$ घंटों में समय है। $t=0$ पर $R=\dfrac{N}{5}$ तथा $t=2$ पर $R=\dfrac{N}{2}$ है। तब $R(3)$ बराबर है
solution_full: The model is $\dfrac{dR}{dt}=kR(N-R)$ with $0<R<N$, $k>0$ a constant.
So $\dfrac{R}{N-R}=\dfrac14\cdot2^{t}$. The ratio doubles every hour: $\dfrac14,\dfrac12,1,2$ at $t=0,1,2,3$.
Option (D) is the linear interpolation; option (C) assumes the curve is symmetric about $t=2$ after one hour.
originality_note: New: a logistic growth problem in which the two data points make the odds ratio R/(N-R) double each hour, read at a time after the midpoint. Closest known: logistic population questions asking when P reaches M/2. Different because: the answer comes from the odds ratio, not from the symmetric half-way time, and the total N is a symbol.
blueprint_concepts: Application problems: growth, decay, Newton's law of cooling, mixtures

concept_use.Application problems: growth, decay, New: The modelling step turns the rumour law into dR/dt = kR(N - R) and the two data points fix the constants (a growth problem).
concept_use.Variable separable equations: The equation is separated with partial fractions and integrated to ln(R/(N - R)) = kNt + c.

key_step: Partial fractions give ln(R/(N-R)) linear in t; two data points fix it; the odds double each hour.
justification: Modelling plus separable integration with partial fractions and two conditions; two ideas linked. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q2 (L3) as an applied modelling question and above the routine 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).
